cells: Removal of loose particles leading to lowering of land surface.
Sand-laden winds polish, groove, and cut rock surfaces.
Particles collide and become smaller and rounded.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Deflation removes fine particles to form landforms such as Deflation Hollows, Blowouts, Lag Deposits, Playas, and Desert Pavement (Reg).
Abrasion involves wind-driven particles scouring rock surfaces, creating Ventifacts, Yardangs, Zeugens, Rock Pedestals, and Inselbergs.
Dreikanter are distinct three-faced ventifact stones created under shifting wind directions.
Yardangs align parallel to prevailing winds, whereas Zeugens form tabular structures capped by resistant rock.
Rock Pedestals (Mushroom Rocks) derive their unique shape from intense near-ground wind abrasion.

blocks.content: • Deflation Hollows – depressions created by intense removal of sediments.
Dreikanter – three-faced ventifacts shaped by shifting winds.
• Desert Pavement (Reg) – surface of coarse pebbles after fine materials are removed.
• Lag Deposits – accumulation of heavier particles left behind after deflation.
• Playas – dry lake beds formed in desert basins.

blocks.content: • Dreikanter – three-faced ventifacts shaped by shifting winds.
• Yardangs – elongated ridges aligned with prevailing winds.

items: Distinguish between Yardangs (elongated ridges aligned with prevailing winds) and Zeugens (tabular ridges with resistant cap rock).
Note that Reg is the alternative term for Desert Pavement left behind after fine materials are deflated.
Rock Pedestals (Mushroom Rocks) are formed specifically due to maximum abrasion occurring near ground level.

blocks.content: • Zeugens – tabular ridges with resistant cap rock.
• Rock Pedestals (Mushroom Rocks) – undercut bases due to intense near-ground abrasion.
• Inselbergs – isolated resistant rock hills rising from desert plains.
